notes:
Lead: pebblegrove.io - mid-stage B2B SaaS (productivity suite for customer ops).

Context: building an in-app assistant embedded in their web app (chat widget + contextual summaries). Primary constraint is latency: designers insist on perceived realtime typing with streaming responses. Team explicitly said: "we need sub-200ms server-to-client for first tokens and smooth streaming for follow-ups". Cost sensitivity: small seed revenue, expect slow ramp; prefer self-serve hosted API, but will consider Dedicated if predictable cost/latency tradeoffs emerge.

Tech details gathered: frontend uses websocket-based widget, average user message length ~20-40 tokens, common query length + context ~250-600 tokens. Expect concurrency spikes during business hours - target 150 req/s peak in month 1, scale to 600 req/s by month 6. Want prefix caching for knowledge snippets, and deterministic reroute to smaller model for low-cost responses.

Security/compliance: SOC2 required for integrations with enterprise customers; plan to support SSO (SAML) in Q3. Data residency not critical today - US-only for now. Audit logs + token-level billing important for cost attribution per product team.

What we've demoed: quickstart via hosted API, streaming chat sample, basic load test (small). Customer feedback: streaming looks good but saw jitter in mid-size (>200ms) due to batch behaviour. They asked about continuous batching controls and ability to reduce batch windows.

Quotes & ask: "If you can show consistent 100-150ms median for first token in our scenario we can move to POC". Wants a short POC: 2-week scoped test with 200k tokens/mo on hosted API, access to simple telemetry dashboard.

Attached/linked: Fireflies recording + Gmail thread for onboarding + pricing deck stub + Jira for SOC2 evidence follow-up. Typical CRM shorthand in notes.
